title: Complete logarithmic-symbol classification of the oriented residual kernel
precise_statement: For N>=2, Delta>1, and the oriented residual A_N=W_N-b_N(Q)I, its kernel is exactly the simultaneous pair-channel intersection k>=l+4. Let J_N=2N(N-1), let V_N be the Vandermonde in centered left variables, and let theta_a=sum_i Z_i^a Xi_i for a=1,...,N-1 be the logarithmic-symbol frame. Dividing a kernel tensor by V_N^4 and applying the physical tensor-to-Hom identification gives precisely a pure differential-order-Q symbol polynomial in the theta_a, with symmetric polynomial coefficients in e_2,...,e_N. Consequently sum_{P,Q} kappa_N(P,Q)x^P y^Q=x^{J_N}/[product_{r=2}^N(1-x^r) product_{a=1}^{N-1}(1-yx^a)]. The kernel is zero unless P>=Q+J_N and is one-dimensional at equality. Every state is reconstructed from V_N^4, this symbol frame and the actual degree-Q reproducing kernel, not a Euclidean replacement. The chiral V_N^4 intertwining parameter shift Delta_alg=Delta+4(N-1) is algebraic and is not a change of physical mass or an isometry.
assumptions: N>=2, Delta>1, finite P,Q>=0; external labels may be reflected to orient the bound, but internal pair labels keep the original right/left convention.
Strict positivity and exact support of every oriented residual pair summand.
Use the real structure of the physical Bargmann metric to identify the right tensor factor with its algebraic dual.
limitations: The result classifies one oriented baseline eigenspace, not the entire finite spectrum.
It is not a quantum-Hall phase identification, a mass-changing unitary map, or a consequence of quartic degree alone.
The count formula uses exact zero conditions; a small positive eigenvalue is not part of this kernel.

title: Exact positive ranks and unaveraged fixed-right-degree asymptotics
precise_statement: The physical positive rank is exactly d_N(P,Q)-kappa_N(P,Q). For N>=4 fixed, Q fixed and P tending to infinity, it is rho_{N,Q}P^{N-3}+O(P^{N-4}), where L_{N,Q}=binom(Q+N-2,N-2), tau_{N,Q}=[y^Q](1-y)^{-(N-2)}(1+y)^{-1}, and rho_{N,Q}=((7 binom(N,2)+NQ)L_{N,Q}+binom(N,2)tau_{N,Q})/[2 N! (N-3)!]. This is an unaveraged coefficient asymptotic. For N=3, d_3=((P+1)(Q+1)+3 epsilon_P epsilon_Q+2 c_P c_Q)/6 with epsilon_j=1 for even j and zero otherwise and c_j=(1,-1,0)_{j mod 3}; kappa_3=sum_{j=0}^Q d_ch(P-12-Q-j), where d_ch(r)=floor(r/6)+1-1_{r mod 6=1} for r>=0 and zero otherwise. The auxiliary size is r_Q=floor((Q+4)^2/4)-2 when P>=Q+2, and the physical positive rank equals r_Q for every P>=2Q+8. Exact coefficient recurrences permit large-index counts without expanding a degree-P state.
assumptions: Delta>1; finite N>=3 and nonnegative right degree Q.
The asymptotic statement fixes N>=4 and Q before taking P to infinity.
The N=3 eventual threshold is sufficient, not asserted to be the earliest stable threshold at each Q.
limitations: Rank counts do not determine positive eigenvalues, projectors or a microscopic scale.
Neither N nor Q is uniform in the displayed fixed-right-degree asymptotic.
An auxiliary zero direction and a physical baseline state remain distinct.

title: Affine pair-support eigenstate lemma
precise_statement: If every pair component of a primary Psi lies only in channels on which gamma_{kl}=a+beta(C_k-C_0)+eta(C_l-C_0), then Psi is an exact eigenstate of the pair sum with g=binom(N,2)a+beta P(N Delta+P-1)+eta Q(N Delta+Q-1). The conclusion follows from the identity sum_{i<j}C_{ij}=C_tot+(N-2)sum_i C_i in each chirality. Different overlapping pair interactions need not commute. The finite global-primary projector preserves a pair-channel cutoff because the global representation commutes with its pair Casimir.
assumptions: Identical positive-discrete-series scalar factors and a finite primary block.
A covariant self-adjoint two-body kernel with the stated affine values on every pair channel actually supporting Psi.
No Einstein formula is needed for the abstract lemma; the physical Einstein model is one application.
limitations: The lemma is sufficient, not a classification of all exact eigenstates or all accidental degeneracies.
A minimum theorem needs the additional sign conditions on every unused pair channel (EX-05).

title: Universal finite-support line, critical doublet, and chiral projected states
precise_statement: Put a=gamma_00,b=gamma_20,c=gamma_11,e=gamma_31. The projected averaged seed Phi_1=Pi_{P,1}Av(z_1w_1z_2...z_P) is nonzero for every P>=1,N>=P+1 and has g=binom(N,2)a+N(c-a)/2+(b-a)(P-1)(N Delta+P)/[2(2Delta+1)]. For P>=3,N>=P-1, Phi_2=Pi_{P,1}Av(z_1^2w_1z_2...z_{P-1}) is nonzero; it has the same g when R=(2Delta+3)(a-b)-(2Delta+1)(c-e)=0. The two are independent for P>=3,N>=P+1. For Einstein values, R=-24Delta(2Delta^2+Delta-4)/[(2Delta-1)(2Delta+5)], whose only physical root is Delta_*=(sqrt(33)-1)/4. The complete N=4,P=3,Q=1 matrix at that mass is -(129+527sqrt(33))I_2/64. The chiral projected seed Pi_L(P)Av(z_1...z_P), 2<=P<=N, is also nonzero and has g=binom(N,2)a+(b-a)P(N Delta+P-1)/[2(2Delta+1)]. Coefficient functionals and their physical Gram duals give the actual states and the selected two-dimensional orthogonal projector.
assumptions: Delta>1 and a covariant pair kernel; the universal formulas use only its displayed low-channel coefficients.
Each seed must exist and lie in the exact stated nonzero range; independence is asserted only on the stated overlap.
The critical-mass value and the explicit 2-by-2 scalar block use the Einstein kernel.
limitations: The universal line remains an eigenvalue above Delta_* but is not then guaranteed to be the lower edge.
Do not extend the nonzero/independence ranges or identify this selected doublet with every degenerate state outside the complete minimum theorem.
No exchange of the fixed-degree Delta contraction with large N or large excitation is established here.
proof_home: Appendix L, §L.5; §L.4 for the complete finite endpoints within the minimum classification

title: Complete finite-N affine minimum multiplicities from root-power inverse systems
precise_statement: The Fischer isometry z^p -> x^p/(Delta)_p carries the physical primary condition to B=sum_i(x_i partial_i^2+Delta partial_i) and the pair cutoff k<=r to (partial_i-partial_j)^{r+1}F=0. Orthogonality to multiplication by S=sum_i x_i identifies the primary slice with the homogeneous quotient by S. The cubic root-power quotient has Hilbert series (1+t)^N-t and the complete subset-module realization; the quartic quotient has series (1+(N-1)t^2)(1+t)^{N-1} and the exact marked-subset module sequence described in Appendix L. Pairing with the right Bose representation gives complete finite-N affine-minimum multiplicity series: 1+t^2(1-t^{N-1})/(1-t) in the chiral sector for every Delta>1; t(1-t^{N-1})/(1-t) in Q=1 for 1<Delta<Delta_*; and (t+t^3)(1-t^{N-1})/(1-t) in Q=1 at Delta_*. At the critical mass the two ladders run through P=1,...,N-1 and P=3,...,N+1, with multiplicity two exactly on 3<=P<=N-1. N=2 has only the critical degrees P=1,3. Exact positive pair defects identify these intersections with the complete lowest eigenspaces.
assumptions: N>=2, Delta>1, finite primary degrees; for N=1 only the chiral degree-zero primary remains and Q=1 intersections vanish.
For the Q=1 minimum statement, use the stated subcritical or critical mass range. Chiral positivity holds throughout Delta>1.
The full root-power ideals and physical Fischer pairing are used, not a proposed low-dimensional subset without a completeness proof.
limitations: The displayed complete minimum formulas are chiral and Q=1 statements, not a classification of arbitrary-Q low spectra.
The quartic root-power result is not generalized to every higher power; for the next cutoff the family (product_i x_i)^2 already disproves the proposed small-family extrapolation at N>=3.
A cutoff subspace need not be invariant under a generic sum of overlapping pair operators.

title: Exact top coefficient, global fixed-N gap, and equality classification
precise_statement: For every fixed N>=2 and Delta>1, the upper coefficient of the full excitation tower is g_top=binom(N,2)gamma_00, carried only by the (0,0) primary and its global descendants. Put c=gamma_00-gamma_20=2Delta(2Delta^2+7Delta+2)/[(2Delta-1)(2Delta+3)]>0. The exact next coefficient is separated by delta g_N=c(N Delta+1)/(2Delta+1), attained only by primaries (2,0),(0,2) and descendants. At full levels (M_L,M_R), the upper multiplicity is one and the gap multiplicity is 1_{M_L>=2}+1_{M_R>=2}. The proof uses strict pair bands g_{n,0}>g_{n,2}>u_n>g_{n+1,0}, u_n=4mu-8(Delta+n)(Delta+n-1), and the stronger comparison gamma_00-gamma_{kl}>=c(1_{k>0}+1_{l>0}), whose equality channels are precisely 00,20,02. Each labelled chiral collision operator K_N=sum_{i<j}(I-P_{ij,0}) has first positive eigenvalue (N Delta+1)/(2Delta+1); triangle summation and its explicit degree-two saturating polynomial give the sharp many-body comparison.
assumptions: N>=2 fixed, Delta>1; the result concerns the entire finite-degree coefficient tower at that fixed particle number.
Use the physical labelled positive-discrete-series Hilbert metric before restricting to diagonal Bose invariants.
The all-index Einstein pair ordering and the three-site physical Gram are inputs established in the same proof appendix.
limitations: No uniform high-energy perturbation theorem or growing-N estimate at fixed nonzero G follows.
A full level with both M_L<2 and M_R<2 contains no gap branch.
This theorem does not assert that the full nonchiral operator is a Markov generator.

title: Physical Dirichlet dictionary, chiral Markov representation, and a scoped nonchiral obstruction
precise_statement: The unitary map U_Delta z^p=p!L_p^{(Delta-1)}(x)/(Delta)_p realizes the Bargmann norm in the Gamma(Delta) measure. Tensor primaries become homogeneous S^P Y_P(x/S) with Dirichlet(Delta,...,Delta) angular measure; descendants have radial Laguerre parameter N Delta+2P-1. The pair Casimir is Delta(Delta-1) minus the Jacobi differential operator, and pair degree zero is conditional Beta averaging. A positive ground-descendant similarity makes the shifted chiral pair operator a reversible Markov generator with Beta-binomial local and Dirichlet-multinomial global stationary laws: the degree-two projector kernel obeys a_0+a_2 q_2(a)q_2(b)>=2Delta(Delta+1)/(2Delta-1)>0. In contrast, the full nonchiral kernel fails to preserve the natural product-Dirichlet positive cone for every Delta>1, already for two particles. For X=2u-1,Y=2v-1,F=X^2Y^2 and L=w-gamma_00 I, LF(0,0)=-12(10Delta^3+29Delta^2+8Delta-14)/[(2Delta-1)(2Delta+1)(2Delta+3)(2Delta+5)]<0. The exact evolved value is [1-2exp(-ct)+exp(-b_22 t)]/(2Delta+1)^2, negative for all sufficiently small positive t on an open positive-measure set. At Delta=2 the derivative is -88/35. A separate negative off-diagonal occupation cycle (312/35)(-528/35)(416/35) rules out a nonnegative off-diagonal generator obtained by invertible diagonal similarity in that particular basis.
assumptions: Delta>1; the explicit nonchiral counterexample uses N=2 and the separately even physical pair channels 00,20,02,22.
The Markov statement specifies its positive similarity and cone; unitarity alone does not transport pointwise positivity.
For pair degree T<2 the degree-two projector is absent.
A labelled odd-channel extension is chosen for the chiral Markov realization; the physical Bose restriction is fixed.
limitations: The natural nonchiral cone obstruction does not exclude an unrelated nonlocal unitary realization with a different positive cone.
It is not a theorem of general nonintegrability or a statement that physical AdS time evolution is a classical stochastic process.
The chiral generator theorem does not extend automatically to both chiralities.
main_home: Chapter 6, §6.7 (Theorem EX-07 and its physical dictionary)

title: Specified labelled Kohno-residue obstruction and limited related algebraic failures
precise_statement: Prescribe all even pair eigenvalues to be the chiral Einstein values on identical labelled positive-discrete-series factors. Allow arbitrary odd pair eigenvalues, a common scalar shift, a common pair-Casimir addition and a nonzero common rescaling. For every Delta>1, no resulting residues Omega_{ij} satisfy [Omega_12,Omega_13+Omega_23]=0 on the full labelled tensor product. The generic Casimir shift is obstructed by exact primary degrees 2,3,4. At beta_*=Delta(2Delta^2+7Delta+2)/[(2Delta-1)(2Delta+1)(2Delta+3)], the old 02 test vanishes; degree-four 04 and 24 equations uniquely determine the odd values with coefficient determinant -3Delta/(2Delta+3). Degree five then has unavoidable commutator -6Delta^2(Delta+1)(Delta+4)^2(3Delta+8)/[(2Delta-1)^2(2Delta+3)(2Delta+5)]<0 (equal to -64 at Delta=2). Related finite facts have narrower scope: at N=4,Delta=2,P=6,Q=0 the two chiral low-channel sums have rank-two commutator and scalar common commutant; at N=3,Delta=2, [W_3,D_2]p_2=-64p_3/7. The chiral plateau with only two nonzero low-channel deviations also excludes one global fixed polynomial or nonsingular rational function of the pair Casimir.
assumptions: The prescribed even coefficients are exactly the Einstein chiral pair values at a fixed Delta>1.
The relation is the labelled three-site infinitesimal braid/Kohno relation; all pair-odd channels remain available.
The common shift, Casimir coefficient and odd values may depend on the chosen mass; the rescaling is nonzero.
The finite commutant and D_2 statements are confined to the explicitly stated blocks and operators.
limitations: This excludes the prescribed two-site residue ansatz, not arbitrary Bethe ansatze, unrelated spectral-parameter constructions, nonlocal changes of variables, or every notion of integrability.
The finite common-commutant examples do not prove a global classification of conserved charges.
The analytic bulk-charge obstruction has a separate proof home and hypotheses in the SC appendix; it is not subsumed by EX-08.
main_home: Chapter 6, §6.8 (Theorem EX-08 and adjacent scoped obstructions)
proof_home: Appendix O, §§O.2–O.4; Chapter 6, §6.8 for the finite commutant, D_2 and plateau arguments

title: A physical finite quintic has Galois group S5
precise_statement: At Delta=2,N=3,P=6,Q=3, with x=g+240, the physical finite characteristic polynomial contains f_5(x)=3713039955625x^5-942938552055500x^4+74501974772024800x^3-2003576214981165440x^2+19936439419181140992x-54992948200676982784. Its square-free reductions at primes 23 and 17 have factor degrees 5 and (2,3), respectively. Thus f_5 is irreducible, its Galois action is transitive of prime degree and hence primitive, and it contains a transposition (the cube of the 2,3-cycle element). Conjugates of that transposition define a connected invariant graph and generate S5, so Gal(f_5/Q)=S5. This nonsolvable factor rules out a general expression by radicals for all physical finite eigenvalues; an exact polynomial plus isolating interval remains a complete answer.
assumptions: The explicitly specified rational-mass physical finite block and energy shift.
The displayed polynomial is an exact factor of that block, and the reductions have nonzero leading coefficient and are square-free at the indicated primes.
Use the ordinary characteristic-zero Galois action on the five roots.
limitations: No claim is made that every finite block has a full symmetric Galois group.
The supplementary S6 block is retained provenance, not needed for the S5 radical obstruction.
Failure of radical formulas is not failure of a complete exact algebraic algorithm and is not a theorem of dynamical nonintegrability.
proof_home: Appendix O, §O.1; Chapter 6, §6.8 for the exact polynomial and prime cycle types

title: Exact stable affine pencil and averaged occupation normalization
precise_statement: For N>=max(1,P+Q), W_N=gamma00 choose(N,2)+N A+B on the fixed centered primary algebra. A is a triangular derivation and B has order<=2. The averaged occupation map is prod h_alpha^(n_alpha/2)/sqrt(N!) times the canonical occupation creation monomial, with Gamma_s=g_s/(N)_downarrow r_s.
assumptions: Unique zero excitation
Conserved nonnegative excitation bidegrees
Number-preserving two-body pair operator
Global covariance for the primary restriction

title: Analytic Hermitian N^-1/2 theorem
precise_statement: For every fixed primary block and Delta>1 there is a regular analytic orthonormal frame in t=N^-1/2. Its matrix is Hermitian for real t near zero; eigenvalues and orthonormal eigenvectors have convergent Taylor series in t. g_j=gamma00 choose(N,2)+N sum_m lambda_jm N^(-m/2). Simple leading branches are even; degenerate clusters can exchange under parity.
assumptions: Fixed P,Q and Delta>1
Stable N sufficiently large
limitations: No uniform radius across all degrees/masses; no assertion that every odd coupling splits eigenvalues.

title: Actual leading Jordan resonance and exact (4,1) branches
precise_statement: The complete stable (4,1) leading matrix is the displayed triangular 3x3 with delta=d^2F/(2D4), F=2d^3-37d^2-11d+100 and v>0. F has two roots >1 in the displayed rational intervals. At either root A-s0I is nonzero rank-one square-zero, Jordan type (2,1). The exact invariant 2x2 plane has k>0 and yields a nonzero +/-sqrt(kv N) split and the stated detuning law.
assumptions: Delta>1
At resonance or the stated local detuning for the half-power formula

title: All-bidegree generic linearization
precise_statement: Outside a countable algebraic set of Delta>1, triangular polynomial eigenvariables u_pq put A=sum sigma_pq u_pq partial_u_pq in every degree. Each cutoff has finitely many exceptions. The nonidentity of every genuine-splitting divisor follows from residue rho_pq=(3/2)(2 f_p f_q-1) at d=1/2 and v2(rho_pq)=-[2(p+q)-s2(p)-s2(q)].
assumptions: Einstein rational channel family
Each generator degree at least two
Generic fixed physical mass
limitations: No local finiteness of the full exceptional set, no classification of all resonances, no simultaneous diagonalization of B.

title: Einstein chiral low algebra and oblique retraction
precise_statement: For Q=0, N>=P>=2, K=A-(sigma2/2)E has semisimple zero kernel C[c2,c3], with all other eigenvalues positive. q=lim exp(-tau K) exists degreewise and is multiplicative. The exact minimum is gamma00 choose(N,2)+(P sigma2/2)N+(beta2/2)P(P-1).
assumptions: Delta>1 fixed
Stable chiral block

title: Einstein Gegenbauer first low operator
precise_statement: B_low=(beta2/2)E(E-1)+(epsilon/2)(y^2+4x^3)partial_y^2 with the exact positive rational epsilon in §9.5. Monic polynomials F_b satisfy J F_b''=b(b-1)F_b; x^a F_b, 2a+3b=P, have gap epsilon choose(b,2). The Gegenbauer parameter is -1/2.
assumptions: Delta>1
Fixed chiral degree
Einstein exact channels

title: Convergent integer expansions only for the isolated chiral low cluster
precise_statement: For each fixed P and Delta>1, the # {2a+3b=P} isolated lowest leading branches have convergent integer 1/N expansions, g=g_min+epsilon choose(b,2)+eta(a,b)/N+O(N^-2).
assumptions: Fixed P>=2, Delta>1
Einstein chiral low cluster
limitations: Remainder not uniform when P grows with N.

title: Exact third-order C2 and all first energy corrections
precise_statement: In graph gauge qOmega=I, C2=-qBRB with R=K^-1(1-q). C2=J[r0 partial_y^2+r1 partial_x^3+r2 x partial_x partial_y^2+r3 y partial_y^3], with the full rational r_i table in Appendix ST-C.4. Its Gegenbauer diagonal is eta(a,b) in §9.6, including the listed Delta=2,P=12 values.
assumptions: Fixed Einstein chiral degree and Delta>1

title: Protected (3,1) discriminant-square doublet
precise_statement: In the stable two-dimensional (3,1) block, the exact shifted pencil has discriminant delta31^2(N+6beta)^2. At Delta*=(sqrt33-1)/4 it is scalar with the displayed energy coefficient and multiplicity two. This is not the nonzero Jordan collision of ST-03.
assumptions: Complete (3,1) stable block

title: Exact chiral character and persistent cusp quotient
precise_statement: For any real chiral pair sequence, L(c_p)=(1-p)t^p is a nonzero exact left character at degree P>=2, with L A=sdP L and L B=sP(P-1)L. On C[x,y], kernel L=(y^2+4x^3). The quotient is preserved at every effective order after subtracting the exact scalar.
assumptions: Stable creation algebra
Same covariant pair representation
No positivity needed for the character

title: Fixed-degree oscillator contraction
precise_statement: With x_i=sqrt(Delta)z_i and degree fixed, Delta^p p!/(Delta)_p->p!, (w_chiral+4Delta^2)/Delta->relative-degree-zero projector, epsilon/Delta->27/34, and the first low gap divided by Delta tends to 27b(b-1)/68.
assumptions: Excitation degree fixed before Delta->infinity
Chiral pair operator and first low layer
limitations: No interchange with growing-degree limits or equality of finite-mass physical models.

title: Common-support kernel and principal-symbol class
precise_statement: For w_kl=u-c min(Ck,Cl)+epsilon_|k-l|(min), c>0, epsilon0,epsilon2>0 and higher even epsilon=0, the oriented residual has exactly the Einstein positive bad support and hence identical full kernel, Hilbert series and rank. If sup_(n<=L) epsilon0,2(n)=o(L^2), the Grassmannian symbols agree with coefficient 8 replaced by c.
assumptions: Same unitary global scalar representation
Real symmetric allowed pair coefficients
Growth only for symbol statement
limitations: Identical kernel does not fix positive eigenvalues or symbol.

title: Compactness does not imply finite Schatten summability
precise_statement: The diagonal chiral tail v_k=1/log(k+2), k even, is c0 and selfadjoint. Its connected resolvent at 2 has entries v_k/[2(2-v_k)]>=v_k/4 and belongs to no finite Schatten S_s.
assumptions: Abstract pair operator
Every finite s>0
limitations: Does not refute extra Einstein-specific Schatten estimates.

title: First positive affine defect theorem
precise_statement: If all even affine defects r_k>=0 and the first positive one is k*=2m+2, then g*=gamma0 choose(N,2)+sP(Nd+P-1) is the exact stable chiral minimum, and K=A-sd E has semisimple kernel C[c2,...,c_(2m+1)] with all other leading gaps positive. q=lim exp(-tau K) is an algebra retraction.
assumptions: Nonnegative affine defects
First positive defect exists
limitations: Nonnegative defects are not necessary for the leading-kernel conclusion: UN-06.

title: General two-generator coefficient from channels four and six
precise_statement: For r4=v>0,r6=w>=0 and nonnegative later defects, B_low=sE(E-1)+epsilon/2 J partial_y^2, epsilon=27vw(d+3)(d+4)(2d+9)/[2(2d+5)(15(2d+7)(d+5)v+(2d+3)(d+2)w)]. Higher defects do not enter. If w>0 the first low spectrum is simple and integer branches follow. If w=0 the first gap is identically zero.
assumptions: Two-generator low retraction exists
Nonnegative-defect theorem provides its sufficient hypotheses

title: Same support and symbol with four low generators
precise_statement: At d=2, w_kl=16-8min(Ck,Cl)+1_(spin0)+(9/14)1_(spin2) has the Einstein kernel/rank and principal symbol, but s=-1/28,r4=0,r6=13/14 and leading low algebra C[c2,c3,c4,c5]. The complete stable P4Q0 matrix is [choose(N,2)-2N/7-3/7] I_2.
assumptions: Abstract selfadjoint pair deformation
N>=4 for the explicit block

title: Signed defects preserve the same leading kernel
precise_statement: At d=2, r4=1,r6=-1/100, all other even defects zero, every high leading gap is positive because alpha_(p,6)/alpha_(p,4)=28(p-5)(p-4)/[11(p+8)(p+9)]<28/11. Thus K has the same semisimple C[c2,c3] kernel in every degree despite a negative defect; its generic epsilon is negative.
assumptions: Abstract affine-subtracted chiral pair sequence
p>=6 for the ratio, p=4,5 separately positive

title: Minimal residue class for generic leading linearization
precise_statement: For pair coefficients rational over Q(d), if gamma00 has a nonzero simple residue R at d=1/2 and every other channel is regular there, the slope residue is R(2f_pf_q-1). The common R cancels from homological relations, giving the same all-degree nonidentity proof and countable algebraic exceptional set.
assumptions: The stated pole structure
Same endpoint representation weights
Rationality over Q(d) for algebraic exceptional roots
